summary.tagline: In the three main towns of the Gastein Valley, Alpine life can be experienced in many ways throughout the year

days.title: Historical Center and Rock Spas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Bad Gastein
stops.detail: Bad Gastein impresses with its Belle Époque architecture and roaring waterfalls.

stops.name: Felsentherme
stops.detail: At the Felsentherme in Bad Gastein you bathe in it inside the rock itself, across four separate spa areas, with the surrounding mountains in view.

stops.name: Gastein Healing Gallery (Heilstollen)
stops.detail: The water is used at the Felsentherme in Bad Gastein, the Alpentherme in Bad Hofgastein and the Gastein Healing Gallery (Heilstollen).

days.title: Alpine Leisure and Thermal Waters
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Bad Hofgastein
stops.detail: Bad Hofgastein offers family-friendly trails, bike parks and small mountain lakes.

stops.name: Alpentherme
stops.detail: The Alpentherme in Bad Hofgastein has water areas, saunas and quiet rooms.

stops.name: Gamskarkogel
stops.detail: The highest peak in the area is the Ankogel (3,252 m), while within the valley the Gamskarkogel (2,467 m) dominates the landscape.

days.title: Natural Wonders and Quiet Paths
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Dorfgastein
stops.detail: Around Dorfgastein, you’ll find quiet Alpine paths, historic mills and regional cuisine.

stops.name: Gadaunerer Gorge
stops.detail: Many of them can be visited – the Gadaunerer Gorge, the Entrische Kirche show cave, the glacial mills above Bad Gastein.
